approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds molecular graphs from a bounded population of accepted high-scoring molecules, using score-quantile parent sampling, connected-fragment crossover and local graph mutations. Its retained mutations include formula-preserving relocation of aromatic nitrogen, and stable identity checks admit a surplus pool of novel candidates. A Gaussian process trained on all earlier accepted scores uses integer counts of local molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity to predict that pool jointly. The Parent chooses each evaluation by taking a fresh correlated posterior draw's highest available candidate, then admits accepted feedback to its prediction archive and breeding population.
approach.novelty: Add explicit batch-best allocation. Build one shared panel of posterior function draws and choose each next molecule by how much it raises the panel's average best score among the molecules already selected. This lets the remaining evaluations cover high-outcome possibilities that the current batch has not captured. Earlier siblings changed survival, parent allocation, graph production, identity admission or posterior features and noise; they have not optimized the utility of the selected batch as a set. The new rule retains the Parent's count posterior and tests a different use of its predictions, with a fixed 128-path numerical panel and separately measured real search outcomes.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent n-559d25e9c9c7 makes each batch-position choice from a separate joint posterior draw, masking previously chosen identities but never valuing the next molecule by what the selected batch already covers. Its complete supplied summaries and run logs give macro mean 0.574343936523512 and population SD 0.012316775530180069, with paired changes against its own Parent of +0.044871389447797005, -0.00466084980236503 and +0.027509304961639947. All formal emissions are valid and novel, yet only 624 of 4350 offspring strictly beat their best generating parent, with 241 incumbent improvements. The current count posterior has useful selected-stream prediction and rank association, but its Curate observation records latent interval coverage of 76.9 percent overall and 33.3 percent on sitagliptin, so posterior tail values cannot be treated as calibrated outcomes. A passive audit reconstructs all 435 original draw selections and 3760 same-mask departures from posterior mean. Its ten-row panels also reveal an important limit: the Parent's ten selected identities already include a global maximizer for every one of those ten paths, so replacing their selection with greedy maximization on that same tiny panel supplies no improvement claim. The proposed numerical panel therefore has 128 paths, fixed before the supplemental audit. On 255 eligible fixed Parent archives and pools, the supplemental audit concatenates the current and following already recorded standard-normal rows, reconstructs the unchanged count posterior, and reproduces the original ten function rows with maximum absolute error 5.85e-14. It uses no later identity or score in those fits and excludes the last twelve batches of each session, which lack enough remaining recorded normals. Among 2295 later positions, the actual Parent choice has marginal contribution at most 1e-12 to this 128-path batch-maximum estimate while an available alternative exceeds 1e-12 in 145 cases. The registered greedy rule changes 254 of 255 selected sets and 2387 of 2550 positions; its same-panel expected maximum rises in 245 batches, ties within 1e-12 in ten, and never falls, with mean difference +0.006404560072195648 in score units. This is an internal decision comparison, not an oracle result or an executed Child trajectory. Mean selected uncertainty increases from 0.0369636 to 0.0391079, while mean pairwise conditional correlation also increases from 0.0381594 to 0.0424568; reduced covariance or chemical redundancy is therefore not the claimed prerequisite. The target limitation is absence of explicit incremental batch-best utility. The earlier n-fc2c108a5253 observation and cluster c-1e7b33da25 established uncertainty-dependent pool choices but weak parent-beating yield and no isolated acquisition contribution. Reproducible passive audit artifacts are runs/SPIRAL2/policy/responses/r0012-04-improve-L01-plan.audit.py and .audit.json, and r0012-04-improve-L01-plan.panel128.audit.py and .audit.json.
hypothesis: Allocate the announced batch by greedy maximization of a shared Monte Carlo estimate of the posterior expected maximum over the selected pool members, so each added molecule is valued by its incremental contribution to the batch's predicted best outcome.

finding_summary.headline: Batch utility changes selection and raises offspring yield, but final mean score does not improve
finding_summary.insights:
The missing batch-set objective was a real decision difference, but correcting it did not supply the registered final-score benefit. This rules out lack of allocation opportunities or a nonexecuting selector as explanations for the result. It also shows why more parent-beating offspring and more incumbent updates are insufficient evidence of stronger final solutions: they can be more frequent increments along a weaker search history. Here the absolute batch-best scores declined even as those counts rose.

The higher internal objective describes the same finite posterior panel used to choose the batch. It does not reveal the real scores of the unevaluated alternatives. The posterior model itself is unchanged; the lower prediction MSE reflects a changed selected stream and feedback history, and does not establish repaired uncertainty. Coverage remains especially poor on sitagliptin, at 37.4%. Model error, limited tail sampling and the objective’s focus on the next batch rather than future breeding remain plausible limits. Those explanations need separate evidence; the current paired panel does not identify their individual contributions. Greedy maximization is also approximate: on the Parent’s original ten-path panels, its existing batches already captured every path maximum and a passive greedy replacement sometimes lost internal utility.

The molecular assessment finds recognizable ring-rich families alongside recurrent reactive heteroatom bonds, unusual ring closures and unassigned stereochemistry. The slightly narrower core coverage and higher same-pool correlation show that batch-best complementarity need not mean broader or cleaner chemistry. Valid graphs and higher posterior batch utility therefore leave chemical feasibility unresolved. The supported finding is successful allocation activation with no demonstrated final-score gain on these three seeds; transfer to different posterior quality, chemical families or batch sizes remains open.
finding_summary.results:
The batch objective changed the selected set in 434 of 435 batches when compared with the Parent rule on the same candidate pools and posterior draws. Among 3,765 later positions with a distinct positive-gain winner, 3,440 choices differed from the corresponding raw-draw winner under the same mask. Every emitted choice matched the registered acquisition. The internal estimate of the batch maximum rose by 0.00597 on average against the Parent comparator: 418 batches improved, 17 tied and none declined. The finite panel still saturated: 150 later positions across 45 batches had exactly zero gain and followed the declared index tie rule.

On the actual scored searches, strict improvements over the best generating parent rose from 624 to 688 out of 4,350 offspring, and incumbent improvements rose from 241 to 298. Yet the average accepted batch-best score fell from 0.48731 to 0.46096. The three-seed final macro mean was 0.57398 versus 0.57434 for the Parent, a change of -0.00036, below the required +0.002 improvement. One seed improved and two fell; seven of fifteen task/seed endpoints improved. Mean endpoints rose for sitagliptin and median similarity, while decoration hopping, DRD2 and zaleplon declined. Every session completed with valid, novel emissions and no numerical fallback.

Selected-stream prediction MSE fell from 0.01127 to 0.00980, while mean within-batch rank correlation fell from 0.550 to 0.515. Nominal 95% latent intervals covered only 77.6% of outcomes, versus 76.9% for the Parent. On identical Child pools, the changed rule selected slightly more uncertainty than the Parent rule, but average conditional correlation increased slightly and distinct molecular cores fell from 7.17 to 7.06 per batch.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families with cyclic amines and amides, but recurrent reactive bonds, unusual ring closures and unassigned stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: All five objectives have complete supplied trajectories; the brief lists no tasks_without_trajectories. The output contains compact methoxyaryl heterocycles, extensively decorated nitrogen heterocycles, flexible diaryl cyclic amines, medium-ring polyamides, and fluorinated carbonyl-rich heterocycles. These are predominantly connected ring-containing molecules, with occasional tiny fragments. The digest ring-closure rates range from 0.9506 to 0.9793 and aromatic-token rates from 0.9333 to 0.9747; these are fractions of proposal strings containing those features, not aromatic atom fractions or evidence of conventional ring geometry. All 4350 optimizer occurrences parse as single connected molecules in passive RDKit 2023.09.6 checks. This establishes graph validity only. Many accepted graphs contain nitrogen-halogen or oxygen-halogen bonds, peroxide links, dense thione chemistry, or short bridges across aromatic systems. Useful ordinary medicinal-chemistry motifs are present, especially non-acylated cyclic amines, aryl ethers and amides, but their coexistence with these liabilities makes overall synthetic plausibility questionable and drug-likeness weak. Structural diversity is moderate across the supplied seeds and objectives, with recognizable families dominating the high-score excerpts; high string uniqueness does not establish broad chemically plausible scaffold coverage. Every task has a zero digest stereocentre rate, although passive perception finds unassigned tetrahedral centres in many proposed graphs. Compared with parent n-559d25e9c9c7, the families remain recognizable while ring topology and heteroatom attachments change; the task entries describe those chemical differences alongside existing recorded scores without attributing activation or assigning new scores. All passive sizes, bond counts and perceived ring sizes below come from the supplied trajectories and are recorded in the accompanying molecular.audit.json. Digest best examples are pooled across seeds, whereas its final examples are the last listed seed-2 evaluations; those final examples are proposals, not a claim that the incumbent was lost.

per_task.generated_character: The optimizer mainly produces compact aromatic nitrogen compounds: median 25 heavy atoms, with a digest mean SMILES length of 41.5 and ring/aromatic-token rates of 0.9506/0.9437. The initial methoxyindole arylamide scores 0.3051048083696145. One high-score family retains indole-like rings and an arylamide but attaches fluorine to the amide nitrogen and halogen to the pyrrolic nitrogen. The pooled best molecule instead has 26 heavy atoms, two benzene rings, a benzene-fused four-member nitrogen ring, methoxy groups, a nitrile, a formamidine-like substituent and an N-chloro aryl enamine; its perceived ring sizes are 4, 6 and 6. This is ordinary fragment vocabulary assembled into a chemically unusual architecture. Relative to the parent, the median heavy-atom count remains 25, but nitrogen-halogen-containing proposals increase from 102/870 to 500/870. The parent endpoints are mainly indole/arylcarboxamide variants and a more extensively closed arylamide system; the child adds the nitrile-bearing small-ring family. The corresponding recorded parent-to-child endpoints, in seed order, are 0.45766047024715 to 0.43299980873877003, 0.4423126980074005 to 0.4519753205796759, and 0.4484138510190879 to 0.4586023950591373.
liabilities: N-F, N-Cl and N-Br attachment is recurrent, including halogenated amide and pyrrolic nitrogens; these are reagent-like bond environments rather than an established stable analogue series.

The best scaffold combines a benzene-fused four-member nitrogen ring with an enamine and formamidine-like group. Feasible synthesis and persistence of this assembly are not established by sanitization.
The final O-Br example adds a reactive oxygen-halogen bond while scoring substantially below its methoxy relative.
missing_features: The favorable nitrile/ring-nitrogen/methoxy combination is not preserved consistently in late proposals; the cited amino, ring-carbon and O-Br changes lose score.

A comparably scoring realization of that compact aromatic and polar arrangement with conventional, non-halogenated nitrogen bonding is not demonstrated by the pooled best excerpt. Its score benefit remains untested.
The best small-ring scaffold contains an unassigned tetrahedral centre. No configuration-resolved alternatives are supplied, so stereochemical preference cannot be inferred.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Small fragments such as the cited ethene and dibromine have score 0.0, whereas the connected aromatic heterocycles reach 0.4586023950591373. There are informative close comparisons: the best N-chloro, N-bromo and N-fluoro congeners all have exactly that score, so halogen identity within this set is not a demonstrated preference. Replacing the nitrile by an amino group in the cited N-bromo scaffold gives 0.2933971259571244. Replacing its embedded ring nitrogen by carbon in the N-chloro scaffold gives 0.4005880245850623. In the related saturated side-chain scaffold, replacing a methoxy group by O-Br gives 0.23618327637050734 versus 0.457118710172062 for the methoxy analogue. These comparisons support retaining the particular nitrile, ring-nitrogen and methoxy arrangement within this family; they do not establish that N-halogen reactivity is necessary.

per_task.generated_character: This is the largest and most heavily decorated output family: median 43 heavy atoms, mean SMILES length 90.8, and ring/aromatic-token rates of 0.9713/0.9678. The pooled best example has 39 heavy atoms and perceived ring sizes 4, 4, 6, 6, 6 and 6. It combines an aromatic core and an adjacent-nitrogen heteroaromatic ring with an N-rich thione heterocycle, exocyclic unsaturation, fluorinated amino substituents and strained annulations. The final seed-2 family instead contains linked nitrogen heteroaromatics, a benzene-fused lactone, carbamate/formamide groups and oxygen-rich chains carrying aldehydes, peroxides or O-F attachments. Across the full child stream, 224/870 proposals have an oxygen-halogen bond, 110/870 have an O-O bond, and 240/870 have a perceived three- or four-member ring. The parent already had large decorated assemblies and reactive oxygen chains; its corresponding counts were 113/870, 164/870 and 18/870. The mean heavy-atom count changes from 51.13333333333333 to 48.57011494252873 while the median changes from 41 to 43, so this is not a uniform shift toward compact molecules. Recorded parent-to-child endpoints are 0.6092799188640974 to 0.616571018651363, 0.6199818405862896 to 0.5942318675042833, and 0.616992140985949 to 0.6074025115664243. The parent seed-2 endpoint had 30 heavy atoms; the child seed-2 endpoint has 48 and an O-O-containing appendage.
liabilities: The best structure combines multiple thiones, a fluorinated carbon attached to several nitrogens, imine/enamine-like groups and small fused rings; the combination warrants a substantially stronger feasibility argument than its valid graph provides.
The final family carries O-O, O-F, aldehyde and nitroso functionality in highly decorated molecules. These are structural reactivity concerns; no stability or toxicity measurement is supplied.
Size remains poorly bounded chemically: the optimizer reaches 119 heavy atoms, and its seed-1 endpoint contains 81 heavy atoms with extensive unsaturated decoration.
missing_features: Compact, chemically conservative alternatives that preserve the favorable connected heteroaromatic arrangement are poorly represented in the best child excerpt; the parent seed-2 endpoint demonstrates that a smaller architecture can receive a comparable recorded score.

The excerpt does not resolve which peripheral donor, acceptor and ring substitutions matter: many differently decorated structures share the same recorded score. Stable replacements for peroxide, oxygen-halogen and densely unsaturated appendages are an untested chemical capability, not an inferred objective requirement.
Configuration-defined versions of the fluorinated and annulated structures are absent; no stereochemical reward can be read from these trajectories.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The cited fluorine, interhalogen and small carbonyl examples sit at the observed floor of 0.5. The initial fused heterocycle/aryl ester scores 0.548381482770623, and the decorated ring-rich products reach 0.616571018651363. This supports a preference for some connected heteroaromatic architecture over tiny fragments, but does not identify a unique decoration requirement. The digest contains many chemically different side-chain and annulation variants tied at 0.616019768563163. The final peroxide/O-F structure still scores 0.606951871657754, and the nitroso/peroxide example scores 0.6036414565826331. Those observations show that chemically consequential appendages can be tolerated within a narrow score band; they do not establish useful reactivity or synthetic viability. The lower endpoint of the much larger seed-2 child also gives no support for indiscriminate growth as a favorable feature.

per_task.generated_character: The high-score family consists of substituted diaryl molecules joined through flexible aliphatic chains and non-acylated cyclic amines. The optimizer median is 32 heavy atoms; digest mean SMILES length is 58.0, and ring/aromatic-token rates are 0.9644/0.9632. The best example has 31 heavy atoms, two benzene rings, a tertiary azetidine nitrogen, methoxy and O-NH2 groups, aromatic halogens and a benzylic chloride. Its perceived rings are 4, 6 and 6; it is not a piperazine scaffold. Nearby high scorers exchange the O-NH2 group for methoxy or O-Br, or add a primary amine. The final seed-2 family contains bridged saturated diamines, aryl thiols and frequently a sulfur centre bearing both C=S and S=S double-bond representations. The parent likewise reached diaryl non-acylated amines, including more conventionally sized saturated rings. Child versus parent counts are 454/870 versus 9/870 for perceived three- or four-member rings and 204/870 versus 86/870 for oxygen-halogen bonds. Recorded parent-to-child endpoints are 0.9959491085611949 to 0.9974355450101015, 0.9964552366323939 to 0.9913558178631674, and 0.9912887882944748 to 0.9895007716676499. The high-score amine/diaryl arrangement persists while the ring and appendage chemistry changes.
liabilities: The leading series combines long rotatable linkers, heavy aryl substitution and a benzylic chloride; graph validity alone does not establish useful exposure or stability.
O-Br and N-Br variants occur among high scorers, while final structures add aryl thiols and highly unusual multiply double-bonded sulfur environments.

Azetidines can be synthetically legitimate, but the frequent small and bridged ring assemblies require individual geometric and synthetic assessment. Their presence alone is not a blanket failure criterion.
missing_features: The useful non-acylated cyclic amine is already present; a claim that this generator lacks basic ring nitrogens would contradict the molecules. What is missing is consistent preservation of that arrangement in conventional, well-defined ring systems without questionable appendages.

The high-score diaryl amines are not configuration-defined: the best structure has three unassigned tetrahedral centres, and 833/870 optimizer proposals have an unassigned centre. No stereochemical preference can be inferred.

No reliable score requirement for O-Br, O-NH2 or the unusual sulfur centre is demonstrated; cleaner versions retaining the diaryl/amine geometry remain a transferable chemical direction rather than a target-specific prescription.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The cited low-score ketone/sulfonamide has a sulfonyl-bound ring nitrogen and scores 0.00021169315013374197; the small fluorinated aromatic ether scores 0.0018635782899060198. Neither has the high-score combination of two aryl regions and a freely substituted saturated amine. The initial large acidic sulfonamide scores 0.01904115112334333, so aromatic size or halogenation alone is insufficient in the shown molecules. The ordinary dimethoxy diaryl azetidine reaches 0.9969241385274472; its O-Br relative is 0.9972659759311256 and its O-NH2 relative is 0.9974355450101015. Thus the diaryl/non-acylated-amine arrangement is the strongest visible common feature, while these small differences do not establish a need for reactive oxygen substitution. The final diamine lacking the unusual sulfur double-bond assembly still scores 0.981013411741664. Basicity and protonation are chemical interpretations of nitrogen environment here, not measured pKa values or evidence of a particular binding pose.

per_task.generated_character: The output concentrates on aryl-substituted nitrogen/carbonyl rings with alkyl and ether decoration. The optimizer median is 32 heavy atoms, mean SMILES length is 55.2, and ring/aromatic-token rates are 0.9793/0.9747; halogen-token rate is only 0.108. The best example has 33 heavy atoms and a propyl/ethoxy-substituted phenyl group attached to a ten-member nitrogen ring containing two N-methyl amide carbonyls. Its other aromatic substituent is a nonstandard compact bridged aza/[nH] system: RDKit perceives two five-member cycles sharing a bridging path, not an ordinary fused azaindole. The next cited example replaces that part by an even more constrained aromatic bridge with perceived four-member cycles, alongside a nine-member polyamide ring. A separate high-score family combines a short aryl-oxygen bridge, a phenyl-bearing lactam region and an eight-member nitrogen ring. The parent already produced alkoxyaryl cyclic urea/lactam and polyamide architectures. The child has 409/870 proposals with perceived three- or four-member rings versus 102/870 in the parent, and 431/870 with rings of at least eight atoms versus 393/870. Recorded parent-to-child endpoints are 0.22270606177144964 to 0.2395714363708875, 0.24321515648721753 to 0.21628057414063917, and 0.23035161967494103 to 0.2451042931779277.
liabilities: Short bridges across aromatic systems can sanitize without establishing a realistic geometry. The two five-member perceived cycles in the best terminal heteroaromatic group should not be described as a conventional fused aromatic scaffold.
Medium-ring polyamides and multiply bridged lactams may be makeable individually, but the supplied graphs provide no ring-closure route or conformational feasibility evidence.
The high-score N-O replacement changes ordinary amide bonding without a visible score penalty, illustrating that score similarity does not establish interchangeable chemical stability.
missing_features: The best excerpt does not supply a conventional aromatic ring architecture carrying the same favorable aryl/polyamide arrangement without short, geometrically unusual aromatic bridges. Such chemically conservative alternatives are not established as score improvements.
The favorable ether, alkylaryl and amide connectivity is not retained consistently during ring and bond substitutions; late examples include altered amide environments and aromaticity.
Configuration-defined forms of the medium-ring and bridged products are absent: 779/870 proposed graphs contain an unassigned tetrahedral centre.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The cited methane, difluoromethane and acetylene fragments score 0.0. The initial fused heterocycle/aryl ester scores 0.1678386594791329, while the aryl/medium-ring polyamide assembly reaches 0.2451042931779277. Repeated amide carbonyls, alkyl-substituted aryl groups and appropriately linked nitrogen rings coexist in the higher-score family; this does not mean that adding any amide or ring is favorable. The ten-member polyamide example scores 0.2451042931779277 and the closely related ring-expanded example scores 0.2420342333201952. The N-O-containing replacement also scores 0.2420342333201952 despite changed bond chemistry. The final structure with a contracted nonaromatic carbocycle and changed attachment scores 0.2123251450326003. Together these observations favor retention of the connected aryl/carbonyl/nitrogen arrangement over fragmentation or some topology changes, but do not identify the hidden objective references or prove that the unusual aromatic bridge is chemically necessary.

per_task.generated_character: The dominant output is compact fluorinated nitrogen/carbonyl chemistry derived from fused heterocyclic diones and related ring-reorganized systems. The optimizer median is 28 heavy atoms, mean SMILES length is 51.0, and ring/aromatic-token rates are 0.9517/0.9333. The best example has 27 heavy atoms and formula C16H14F3N5O3. It contains an N-fluorinated nitrogen-rich dione ring, an exocyclic double bond, a bridged aromatic/lactam assembly, carbon-bound fluorines and N-methyl groups; only its benzene ring is perceived as an aromatic ring. Another leading family contains a fluorinated azetidine, a fluorinated heterocyclic dione, a hydroxylated unsaturated carbocycle and a thiol. The best seed-2 excerpt instead uses a more flexible amide/enol-ether-like chain and an S-F bond. The parent was already rich in N-fluorinated dione/imino heterocycles. Its median heavy-atom count is 27 versus 28 in the child; its median aromatic-atom count is 15 versus 9, consistent with the child exploring more nonaromatic ring-reorganized chemistry. Nitrogen-halogen proposals number 534/870 in the parent and 593/870 in the child. Recorded parent-to-child endpoints are 0.6510211907030741 to 0.5980589738951324, 0.4870057305679067 to 0.600551289906133, and 0.6025252354500499 to 0.5700483900567853.
liabilities: N-fluorinated diones/imides dominate much of the proposal stream. These are chemically distinct from carbon-fluorinated medicinal scaffolds and may behave as reactive fluorinating motifs.
The best families add strained azetidines, unusual aromatic bridges, enol/enamine-like unsaturation, thiols or S-F groups. Their synthetic and solution behavior is not established.
Repeated large fused-dione/aryl assemblies consume proposals despite extremely low recorded scores, while substantial local connectivity changes can destroy score even near the favorable size range.
missing_features: The compact carbonyl/nitrogen/fluorine balance visible in the high-score family is not preserved consistently: the stream still produces repeated oversized heterocycles and nearby small molecules with very different recorded scores.

Comparable high-score fluorinated architectures using conventional carbon-fluorine placement and stable nitrogen/oxygen connectivity are not demonstrated by the best excerpt; the observed scores do not establish a need for N-F or S-F bonding.

No configuration-resolved versions of the fluorinated saturated and bridged products are shown. Unassigned tetrahedral centres occur in 529/870 child proposals, and their effect on the objective is unknown.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The large repeated heterocycle/aryl product in the worst excerpt has 59 heavy atoms and scores 5.725865957926842e-51. The initial aryl/fused-dione ester scores 0.0020944534688323298. The leading compact fluorinated products reach 0.600551289906133 and 0.5980589738951324, supporting a strong preference in these trajectories for a bounded heteroatom/fluorine arrangement over repeated large heteroaromatic assemblies. Size alone is not sufficient: the cited late 28-heavy-atom carbon-linked chain scores 0.19196886149180178, and the 29-heavy-atom saturated nitrogen-ring variant scores 0.02741443602854399. The best lactam-containing assembly scores 0.600551289906133, whereas insertion of a carbon between that carbonyl and its ring nitrogen gives 0.5926816636813125. That is a local indication that the carbonyl/nitrogen connectivity matters. Neither the preference for carbon-bound versus nitrogen-bound fluorine nor an exact desired pharmacophore is isolated by these multi-feature comparisons.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Nitrogen-halogen bonds occur in 500/870 proposals in one compact aromatic family and 593/870 in a compact fluorinated family. Another ring-rich family contains oxygen-halogen bonds in 224/870 and O-O bonds in 110/870 proposals. High-score excerpts contain N-F/N-Cl/N-Br analogues with identical recorded scores, and a clean diaryl amine analogue remains near its O-Br relative in score. Thus reactive attachments recur without evidence that every such attachment supplies the favorable chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve favorable molecular architectures while keeping heteroatoms in conventional, chemically persistent bond environments.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically conservative alternatives that retain the connected aromatic, amine and carbonyl architecture while varying substituents within appropriate bond environments. Explore conventional carbon-bound halogens and stable nitrogen/oxygen functionality using task-local observed feedback, without assuming that a high recorded score certifies stability or that all heteroatom-halogen chemistry must be forbidden.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One high-score compact aromatic structure contains a benzene-fused four-member nitrogen ring. Another high-score polyamide contains two perceived five-member aromatic cycles sharing a bridging path; its nearby congener has perceived four-member aromatic cycles. A diaryl amine stream has 454/870 proposals with perceived three- or four-member rings versus 9/870 in the parent, while the polyamide stream has 409/870 versus 102/870. These are changes in ring architecture, not evidence of failed valence parsing.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring generation does not distinguish ordinary accessible ring chemistry from short aromatic bridges and densely constrained closures that merely form valid graphs.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make ring construction sensitive to ring size, bridge placement and a plausible embedding of aromatic atoms, while retaining legitimate small saturated rings. Offer less strained topologies that preserve observed favorable substituent relationships; use actual feedback to discover which alternatives matter rather than imposing an objective-specific scaffold.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest stereocentre rate is 0.0 on every supplied proposal set. Passive perception finds unassigned centres in 833/870 proposals in a diaryl cyclic-amine family, 779/870 in a polyamide family and 529/870 in a fluorinated heterocycle family. The leading diaryl amine alone has three unassigned centres. No configuration-resolved score comparison is present.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator supplies constitutionally varied molecules but no explicitly assigned tetrahedral configurations for the stereogenic structures it creates.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Add the ability to construct and preserve explicit configurations at stereogenic centres when generating or changing molecular graphs. Treat configuration exploration as an untested capability and let available feedback determine its utility; do not infer a preferred stereoisomer from unspecified structures.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The decorated heterocycle stream reaches 119 heavy atoms and ends one seed at 81 heavy atoms. A repeated heterocycle/aryl structure with 59 heavy atoms scores 5.725865957926842e-51, whereas compact 27- and 28-heavy-atom structures in its trajectory receive much larger recorded scores. Yet nearby small structures can also score poorly, and other high-score families contain medium rings and extensive decoration. The favorable property is therefore not a universal small-molecule rule.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output lacks consistent control of size and repeated decoration while retaining the particular functional-group connectivity supported by accepted scores.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support contraction and removal of redundant decoration while preserving the local carbonyl, nitrogen, aromatic and substituent relationships associated with observed score. Maintain access to larger architectures where feedback supports them; the needed capability is controlled simplification and size exploration, not an objective-named size target.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A nitrile-to-amino substitution changes a recorded score from 0.4586023950591373 to 0.2933971259571244, an embedded nitrogen-to-carbon change gives 0.4005880245850623, and methoxy-to-O-Br replacement changes 0.457118710172062 to 0.23618327637050734. Elsewhere, freely substituted saturated amines recur in high-score diaryl structures while a sulfonyl-bound ring nitrogen occurs in the lowest-score excerpt. These observations distinguish nitrogen and oxygen environments rather than merely their presence.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator often changes a useful functional-group role while making nearby graph edits, and the output does not reliably retain the favorable local arrangement.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer transformations that can retain nitrile, ether, non-acylated amine and amide roles, as well as controlled alternatives that change one such role. Use observed same-process feedback to discover which local relationships deserve preservation; do not hard-code a role or motif for an unnamed objective.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
